text:
Two teams that haven't lost in two weeks meet in Anaheim, and both are on five-game win streaks. Nashville arrives on the second night of a back-to-back after Juuse Saros stopped all 30 shots in a 3-0 win at Los Angeles last night, and the Predators are still without Jonathan Marchessault, with Shane Wright now playing beside Kerfoot and Forsberg. Anaheim last played three days ago, a 5-2 win over Pittsburgh in which Cutter Gauthier scored three goals. The Ducks are missing A.J. Greer and Ryan Poehling, and Judd Caulfield has taken Poehling's spot beside Nesterenko and Killorn.

Neither streak looks fully earned. At five on five, Nashville has taken 46% of the expected goals (a measure of chance quality) and Anaheim 45%. The Ducks' 26 goals in their last five came on 17.1 expected, and they give up 3.48 expected goals per 60. They also take 5.2 penalties a game. Nashville's power play creates 0.75 expected goals a game, and Anaheim's penalty kill allows 0.79. In net, projected starters Justus Annunen (NSH) and Laurent Brossoit (ANA) have each played four games. Annunen is at -0.93 goals saved above expected (how many goals he's stopped beyond what the shots predicted) and Brossoit at +0.70.

Gauthier is the headliner at 45% to score. Steven Stamkos (38%) and Filip Forsberg (36%) lead Nashville. Roman Josi is one point from 800 for his career. Our under-the-radar picks are both Predators: Ross Colton, a third-liner whose 3.6 expected goals over his last 10 games rank in the top 2% of depth forwards, and Mavrik Bourque, 41% for a point.
